method.toolingIndependence: Every verdict comes from pypdf and a purpose-written PDF content-stream parser, not from pdf-lib or any lane module, so the factory is not the judge of its own output.
method.failClosedInspection: Each artifact is inspected two ways: a walk of the whole indirect-object graph including an xref sweep for objects orphaned from the page tree, and a byte sweep that matches markers as complete PDF names terminated by a delimiter, applied to the file body with stream payloads blanked and to the decompressed payload of every /Type /ObjStm. No verdict rests on an empty hit list from a file that could not be read.
method.falsePositiveControl: A naive substring sweep for '/AA' fires on subset-font BaseFont names such as /AAAZSD+TimesNewRomanPSMT and on raw TrueType glyph tables. Three families tripped it and were cleared by matching complete PDF names in syntax-bearing regions only.
method.printFlagMethod: pdfminer silently skips the /FlatWidget-* Form XObjects that pdf-lib's flatten() emits, which is exactly where the leaked ink lives, so a layout-level text diff reports no change on the two families that carried the defect. Verdicts instead come from parsing each page content stream, tracking the CTM through q/Q/cm, and reading each flattened widget's own appearance stream, decoding literal and hex string operands alike. Each flattened widget is matched back to a single source widget /Rect by geometry, which is what makes the overlapping-rectangle rule decidable: the ink belongs to one identifiable widget rather than to whichever rectangles happen to contain a point.
limitations: The generator was not re-executed. The released source packs are laid out as STATES/<CODE>/... while the lane drivers expect a private pack tree with per-state STATE_MANIFEST.csv under an Edition-1 prefix, so a faithful re-render could not be reproduced from the released assets. Determinism is therefore supported indirectly and not proven: creation and modification dates are pinned to D:20260101000000Z, no trailer /ID is emitted, recorded artifact hashes match the committed bytes, and 24 of the 47 fixture PDFs are byte-identical across the two independent renders (the other 23 differ exactly where widgets were removed).
Visual rasterisation was not performed; every geometric claim comes from decoded content-stream coordinates.

findings.visibleDefect: The new print-flag rule treats the NoView bit (32) as suppressing print. PDF 32000-1:2008 Table 165 says the opposite: a NoView annotation 'may be printed (depending on the setting of the Print flag)' and is hidden only for on-screen display and interaction. Widgets whose /F is 36 (Print|NoView) therefore print on a paper copy, but D0-v2 removes them before flattening. In this family the two affected widgets are 'enter the type of court' and 'enter the county' (/F=36), whose removal is exactly what this family's own caption_overlap acceptance condition asked for, so the outcome here is correct and no in-shard artifact is harmed. The rule itself is over-broad and can silently drop printing ink in any family that uses Print|NoView for content rather than for guidance.
findings.likelyOwner: D0 scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs readAnnotationFlags; byte-identical on all seven correction branches, so every lane inherits it.
findings.acceptanceCondition: Either partOfFiledAppearance stops treating NoView as non-printing (matching Table 165), or the NoView clause is retained deliberately with the departure from the spec stated in the module and the affected widget population measured across all 253 families so the blast radius is known.
findings.evidenceBasis: Module source read at origin/claude/rcap-d1c-corrections-v2 and confirmed byte-identical across all seven correction branches; /F values read directly from the verified source binaries. Across the 19 shard-1 sources, 1401 widgets total, 29 lack the Print bit, 0 set Hidden, and exactly 4 set Print|NoView -- the two named fields in each of the two Nebraska families.
